title: Guide RNA Library Titration of Cas9 Cell Lines
author: Verity Goodwin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgxujxnw
materials: Follow "Fixing Cell Pellets" protocol found here: https://protocols.io/view/fixing-cell-pellets-bg2fjybn.html

steps.title: Detach and collect Cas9 cells
steps.instruction: Detach adherent Cas9 cells and collect them following protocol "Passaging adherent cancer cell lines" steps 1‑8.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells to obtain 1.25×10⁶ cells in 8 mL complete media, yielding a final concentration of 1.56×10⁶ cells·mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Dilute gRNA library
steps.instruction: Dilute the defrosted gRNA library in complete media as needed; keep on ice and use within 1 hour.

steps.title: Add gRNA library to plate
steps.instruction: Add the volumes of diluted gRNA library specified in Table 1 to the 6‑well plate according to the layout in Figure 1 and mix gently by rocking the plate.

steps.title: Add polybrene to suspension
steps.instruction: Add 6.4 µL polybrene (final 8 µg·mL⁻¹) to the cell suspension and mix with a 10 mL stripette and pipetboy.

steps.title: Seed cells into plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 1.6 mL of the cell suspension (≈2.5×10⁵ cells) into each of four wells of a 6‑well plate and add the additional media volume indicated in Table 1 column 4.

steps.title: Incubate plate
steps.instruction: Place the seeded plate in the incubator.

steps.title: Replace media (Day 2)
steps.instruction: Aspirate old media carefully and add 2 mL fresh complete media to each well without dislodging the cells.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate culture media from the well.
Add 2 mL PBS by angling the pipette at the side of the well.

steps.title: Add TrypLE and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL TrypLE to each well, incubate 3–5 min (extend if needed) at the incubator, and monitor under a microscope until all cells are detached.

steps.title: Add media after detachment
steps.instruction: When cells are detached, add 500 µL complete media to each well, mix by pipetting up and down with a P1000, and wash the well base to ensure cells are fully detached.

steps.title: Collect and centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL cell suspension to a labeled 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min (temperature not specified) using a minifuge inside the MSC, then carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Configure flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Set up the cytometer (e.g., BD LSRFortessa) with parameters FSC‑A, FSC‑W, SSC‑A, and 450/50‑A (BFP).

steps.title: Run mock sample and gate
steps.instruction: Acquire the mock (0) sample, gate debris (FSC‑A vs SSC‑A) and single cells (FSC‑A vs FSC‑W) using a polygon gate; adjust FSC/SSC voltages if needed.

steps.title: Gate BFP‑negative mock cells
steps.instruction: Verify mock cells are BFP‑negative (450/50‑A vs SSC‑A), set a polygon gate on the negative population, and record 10 000 events.

steps.title: Run titrated samples
steps.instruction: Acquire each titrated sample starting with the lowest virus volume (15 µL), record 10 000 events per sample, and calculate infectivity as the percentage of single cells that are BFP‑positive.

steps.title: Export and analyze data
steps.instruction: Export FCS files, analyze with FlowJo using the same gating strategy, and export the percentage of BFP‑positive single cells to an Excel file.

steps.title: Plot titration curve
steps.instruction: In Excel, plot % BFP‑positive cells versus virus volume, determine the virus volume that yields ~35 % transduction (e.g., using the linear portion; example calculation (35‑11.324)/0.5057 = 48.8 µL), and scale up for larger culture areas.
